claim: Bicoid (Bcd) is the first protein identified to function as a morphogen.
source: As the first protein identified to function as a morphogen, Bicoid (Bcd) patterns the cells along the antero-posterior axis in the early embryo of the fruitfly, Drosophila melanogaster (Driever et al., 1989).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Driever et al., 1989.

claim: Bicoid patterns cells along the antero-posterior axis in the early Drosophila melanogaster embryo.
source: As the first protein identified to function as a morphogen, Bicoid (Bcd) patterns the cells along the antero-posterior axis in the early embryo of the fruitfly, Drosophila melanogaster (Driever et al., 1989).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Driever et al., 1989.

claim: Bicoid is maternally deposited and localized at the anterior pole of the embryo in the form of mRNA.
source: Bcd is maternally deposited and localized at the anterior pole of the embryo in the form of mRNA (Frohnhöfer and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1986).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Frohnhöfer and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1986.

claim: Localized Bicoid mRNA is translated upon fertilization, forming a protein gradient with exponential decay in concentration along the antero-posterior axis.
source: This localized mRNA is further translated upon fertilization, forming a protein gradient with exponential decay in concentration along the antero-posterior axis.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Bicoid gradient formation.

claim: Bicoid activates different genes, with more anteriorly expressed genes having lower Bcd binding affinity.
source: Fundamentally acting as a transcription factor, Bcd activates different genes, with the more anteriorly expressed genes having lower Bcd binding affinity (Struhl et al., 1989).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Struhl et al., 1989.

claim: The Bicoid gradient is highly dynamic, with nuclear Bcd concentration constantly changing throughout the first 13 rounds of syncytial cell divisions.
source: Quantitative studies have shown that the Bcd gradient is highly dynamic, with nuclear Bcd concentration constantly changing throughout the first 13 rounds of syncytial cell divisions (Little et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Little et al., 2011.

claim: Precise positional information endowed by Bcd gradient at one single time point suffices to distinguish neighbor cell identities.
source: It has been suggested that precise positional information endowed by Bcd gradient at one single time point suffices to distinguish neighbor cell identities (Gregor et al., 2007a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gregor et al., 2007a.

claim: CRY2::mCh::Bcd transgenics rescue the absence of endogenous Bcd in the dark.
source: We find that in the dark, CRY2::mCh::Bcd transgenics rescues the absence of endogenous Bcd.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing gap gene expression patterns and larval hatching.

claim: Expression patterns of hunchback, giant, krüppel and knirps in CRY2::mCh::Bcd embryos in the dark are reminiscent of wild-type embryos.
source: The expression patterns of four gap genes – hunchback (hb), giant (gt), krüppel (kr) and knirps (kni) – are reminiscent of wild-type embryos when the light-responsive Bcd construct is expressed in an otherwise bcd mutant background (Figure 1B–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B-E.

claim: CRY2::mCh::Bcd embryos in the dark hatch as healthy larvae.
source: These embryos hatch as healthy larvae (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Embryos illuminated with blue light during the first 2.5 hr after egg deposition fail to develop head and thorax structures.
source: In comparison, embryos illuminated with blue light during the first 2.5 hr after egg deposition fail to develop the head and thorax structures (Figure 1H'), resembling that of the bcd knockout phenotype (Figure 1H'').
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 1H'.

claim: Illuminated embryos show strong repression of the anterior, Bcd-dependent, expression of hb, gt and kni.
source: Illuminated embryos show strong repression of the anterior, Bcd-dependent, expression of hb, gt and kni, while their posterior, Bcd-independent counterparts remain intact (Figure 1B'–D').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B'-D'.

claim: The Kr band shifts anteriorly in illuminated embryos compared to the pattern observed in the dark.
source: Furthermore, the Kr band shifts anteriorly compared to the pattern observed in the dark (Figure 1E–E', arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1E-E'.

claim: Light-induced conformational changes did not alter the translation inhibitory capability of Bcd in the cytoplasm.
source: It suggests that light-induced conformational changes did not alter the translation inhibitory capability of Bcd in the cytoplasm (in comparison, Cad boundary shifts anteriorly with decreasing bcd dosages, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Cad gradient does not shift in illuminated embryos.

claim: The spatial distribution of Bcd molecules is not affected by optogenetic manipulation.
source: We further quantified the Bcd gradient under dark and illuminated conditions (Figure 1F–F') and observed no significant change in Bcd profile (Figure 1J), showing that the spatial distribution of Bcd molecules is not affected by our manipulation.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Bcd gradient shown in Figure 1J.

claim: CRY2low embryos show significantly reduced transcriptional persistence of hb when illuminated with a 488 nm laser compared to wild-type embryos.
source: Compared to wild-type embryos - where transcriptional activity of hb in the Bcd-dependent anterior domain persists throughout the interphase of nuclear cycle (n.c.) 13 (7.1 ± 3.2 min; Figure 2A and B, Video 1) - CRY2low embryos show significantly reduced transcriptional persistence when illuminated with a 488 nm laser (3.6 ± 1.1 min; Figure 2A and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data of MS2 reporter shown in Figure 2A and C.

claim: The inhibitory effect on hb transcription becomes more prominent in CRY2high embryos.
source: Such an inhibitory effect becomes more prominent in CRY2high embryos (3.0 ± 0.5 min, Figure 2A and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data of MS2 reporter shown in Figure 2A and D.

claim: The transcription of the posterior hb domain is Bcd-independent and shows no inhibitory effect under illumination.
source: The transcription of the posterior hb domain is Bcd-independent and, reassuringly, we do not observe any inhibitory effect in this domain (4.3 ± 2.0 min, 5.2 ± 3.3 min, and 4.2 ± 2.0 min in control, CRY2low, and CRY2high, respectively; Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data of MS2 reporter shown in Figure 2E.

claim: ChIP-qPCR experiments show comparable CRY2::mCh::Bcd binding in dark or light to native Bcd binding sites.
source: As parallel evidence, ChIP-qPCR experiments show comparable CRY2::mCh::Bcd binding in dark or light to native Bcd binding sites (Figure 2F), with no noticeable unspecific DNA binding caused by light-induced conformational changes (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Light-induced conformational changes cause no noticeable unspecific DNA binding by CRY2::mCh::Bcd.
source: As parallel evidence, ChIP-qPCR experiments show comparable CRY2::mCh::Bcd binding in dark or light to native Bcd binding sites (Figure 2F), with no noticeable unspecific DNA binding caused by light-induced conformational changes (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Low power illumination (0.04 mW) causes a moderate reduction and a slight anterior shift of Eve stripes 1 and 2 expression in a WT background.
source: In a WT background, low power illumination (0.04 mW) causes a moderate reduction and a slight anterior shift of the Eve stripes 1 and 2 expression (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2H and I.

claim: Increasing light power further decreases the expression level of the first two Eve stripes.
source: Increasing light power further decreases the expression level of the first two Eve stripes (Figure 2J and K).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2J and K.

claim: When expressed in a bcd null background, CRY2::mCh::Bcd completely inhibits the expression of the anterior two Eve stripes, even at the lowest light power tested.
source: When expressed in a bcd null background, CRY2::mCh::Bcd completely inhibits the expression of the anterior two Eve stripes, even at the lowest light power tested (Figure 2L–O).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2L-O.

claim: 10 min of illumination at the end of n.c. 14 is sufficient to induce embryonic lethality.
source: Surprisingly, 10 min of illumination at the end of n.c. 14 is sufficient to induce embryonic lethality.
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data showing defective mouthparts.

claim: Cuticle preparation of embryos illuminated for 10 min at the end of n.c. 14 shows defective mouthparts, in particular the pharynx.
source: Cuticle preparation of these non-hatched embryos shows defective mouthparts, in particular the pharynx (Figure 3C and D, arrows).
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Thirty minutes of illumination causes further deterioration in mouth development, with minimal mouth skeleton visible.
source: Thirty minutes of illumination causes further deterioration in mouth development, with minimal mouth skeleton visible (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Extending the illumination window depletes all mouthparts.
source: Extending the illumination window depletes all mouthparts (Figure 3F and G), with the most severe phenotypes observed when illumination encompasses both n.c. 13 and n.c. 14.
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: When illumination encompasses both n.c. 13 and n.c. 14, all thorax segments are lost, with only abdominal denticle belts remaining.
source: Under this condition, all thorax segments are lost, with only abdominal denticle belts remaining (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: A 30 min illumination window spanning n.c. 11 ~ 13 results in severe patterning defects.
source: We find that a 30 min illumination window spanning n.c. 11 ~ 13 results in severe patterning defects (Figure 3I), phenocopying the embryos illuminated during n.c. 13 and 14 (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Bcd-dependent transcription before n.c. 14 is indispensable for initiating its downstream gene cascade.
source: This suggests that Bcd-dependent transcription before n.c. 14 is indispensable for initiating its downstream gene cascade.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that illumination spanning n.c. 11-13 results in severe patterning defects.

claim: Shifting the 30 min illumination period to 10 min earlier results in the recovery of proper thoracic segment patterning.
source: Shifting the 30 min illumination period to 10 min earlier results in the recovery of proper thoracic segment patterning (Figure 3J, arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: When the illumination time window is shifted before n.c. 10, the cuticle patterns become equivalent to those of embryos developing in the dark or wild-type.
source: Last, when the illumination time window is shifted before n.c. 10 (Figure 3M), the cuticle patterns become equivalent to those of embryos developing in the dark (Figure 3C) or wild-type (Figure 3B) and, moreover, the larval hatchability reaches that of dark conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: Persistent Bcd-dependent transcription activity from n.c.10 is required for robust embryonic patterning and embryonic viability.
source: These temporal perturbation experiments reveal that persistent Bcd-dependent transcription activity from n.c.10 is required for robust embryonic patterning, and ultimately embryonic viability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments showing that illumination before n.c. 10 does not affect viability.

claim: Formation of the more posterior, thoracic segments is only perturbed when extended illumination covers n.c.13.
source: In contrast, formation of the more posterior, thoracic segments is only perturbed when extended illumination covers n.c.13, the critical time window for properly initiating the downstream gene cascade.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: Blue-light illumination for 10 min before gastrulation impairs the formation of the clypeolabrum lobe and stomodeum invagination while the expression of the more posterior En stripes remains intact.
source: Blue-light illumination for 10 min before gastrulation impairs the formation of these very anterior structures while the expression of the more posterior En stripes remains intact (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Extending illumination to 30 min prior to gastrulation results in the loss of the next two En stripes marking the mandibular and maxillary segments.
source: Extending illumination to 30 min prior to gastrulation, we observe the loss of the next two En stripes marking the mandibular (Mn) and maxillary (Mx) segments (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 30 min illumination prior to gastrulation results in diminished expression of Deformed, a Hox gene that controls morphogenesis of the mandibular and maxillary segments.
source: Concomitantly, we observe diminished expression of Deformed, a Hox gene that controls morphogenesis of these same Mn and Mx segments (Figure 4D').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4D'.

claim: 50 min of illumination prior to gastrulation results in the loss of expression of Sex Comb Reduced (Scr), the hox gene that regulates development of the labial segment.
source: Similarly, 50 min of illumination prior to gastrulation results in the loss of expression of Sex Comb Reduced (Scr), the hox gene that regulates development of the labial segment (Figure 4E' and E'').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4E' and E''.

claim: Further extending illumination results in anterior cells adopting posterior cell fates, reflected in the ectopic expression of Ultrabithorax (Ubx) and Abdomen-B (Abd-B) in anterior regions.
source: Further extending illumination, we observe that anterior cells adopt posterior cell fates, reflected in the ectopic expression of Ultrabithorax (Ubx) and Abdomen-B (Abd-B) in anterior regions (Figure 4E'', F'' and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F'', arrows).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4E'', F'' and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F''.

claim: In the most severe case, all En segments from the anterior to the second thorax (T2) are missing.
source: In the most severe case, we see that all En segments from the anterior to the second thorax (T2) are missing (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: More anterior cell fates require Bcd-dependent transcription to persist until the very end of n.c. 14.
source: This evidence shows that more anterior cell fates require Bcd-dependent transcription to persist until the very end of n.c. 14.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the sequential disappearance of En stripes from anterior to posterior with prolonged illumination.

claim: Cells in more posterior regions undergo correct fate decisions at earlier stages, regardless of the Bcd transcription activity at later time points.
source: In contrast, cells in more posterior regions undergo correct fate decisions at earlier stages, regardless of the Bcd transcription activity at later time points.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: Illumination during the last 30 min of the blastoderm stage does not affect Hb in neither protein level nor boundary position.
source: Illumination during the last 30 min of the blastoderm stage does not affect Hb in neither protein level nor boundary position (Figure 5B), indicating that Hb expression is independent of the newly synthesized mRNA in the last 30 min of n.c. 14.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Hb expression shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Hb expression is independent of the newly synthesized mRNA in the last 30 min of n.c. 14.
source: Illumination during the last 30 min of the blastoderm stage does not affect Hb in neither protein level nor boundary position (Figure 5B), indicating that Hb expression is independent of the newly synthesized mRNA in the last 30 min of n.c. 14.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that illumination during the last 30 min does not affect Hb.

claim: The Hb protein level remains stable once the hb mRNA amount has exceeded a certain threshold value.
source: This shows that the Hb protein level remains stable once the hb mRNA amount has exceeded a certain threshold value.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Hb expression is independent of newly synthesized mRNA in late n.c. 14.

claim: Extending illumination throughout n.c. 14 (or even earlier) results in deviations of the Hb anterior pattern.
source: However, extending illumination throughout n.c. 14 (or even earlier) results in deviations of the Hb anterior pattern (Figure 5B, arrows; and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B4).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Hb expression shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B4.

claim: The mRNA synthesized prior to n.c. 14 is sufficient to support the formation of the broad Hb gradient.
source: Here, we show that the mRNA synthesized prior to n.c. 14 is sufficient to support the formation of the broad gradient, as demonstrated by the Hb expression profile in embryos illuminated throughout cycle 14 (Figure 5B, ④).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Hb expression shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Transcriptional activity in the first 15 min of n.c. 14 is critical for precise formation of the wild-type Hb expression profile, at both anterior and posterior borders.
source: Transcriptional activity in the first 15 min of n.c. 14 is hence critical for precise formation of the wild-type Hb expression profile, at both anterior and posterior (driven by the stripe enhancer) borders.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: Continuous illumination throughout n.c. 13 and n.c. 14 severely impairs the anterior Hb expression level.
source: Further, continuous illumination throughout n.c. 13 and n.c. 14 severely impairs the anterior Hb expression level (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B5), showing that mRNA synthesized during n.c. 13 contributes significantly to the final Hb pattern.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Hb expression shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B5.

claim: mRNA synthesized during n.c. 13 contributes significantly to the final Hb pattern.
source: Further, continuous illumination throughout n.c. 13 and n.c. 14 severely impairs the anterior Hb expression level (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B5), showing that mRNA synthesized during n.c. 13 contributes significantly to the final Hb pattern.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that continuous illumination throughout n.c. 13 and n.c. 14 severely impairs Hb expression.

claim: Recovering the transcriptional activity during the last 30 min of n.c. 14 by reverting the embryos to the dark results in a partial rescue of Hb anterior expression.
source: Interestingly, recovering the transcriptional activity during the last 30 min of n.c. 14 by reverting the embryos to the dark, results in a partial rescue of Hb anterior expression (Figure 5C, arrow), supporting the presence of a hb mRNA threshold.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Hb expression shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Transcription activity in late n.c. 14 fails to recover the stripe enhancer activity.
source: Nevertheless, transcription activity in late n.c. 14 fails to recover the stripe enhancer activity (Figure 5C, ⑥), potentially due to shifted borders of posterior repressive factors.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Hb expression shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Illumination during n.c. 10–12 results in a steep but narrow Hb gradient, where the posterior boundary shifts anteriorly by ~10% EL.
source: Illumination during n.c. 10–12 results in a steep but narrow Hb gradient, where the posterior boundary shifts anteriorly by ~10% EL (Figure 5D, ⑦).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Hb expression shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Illumination carried out before n.c. 11 results in a recovery of the shape of the Hb gradient when comparing to that of dark conditions, although the posterior border is still anteriorly shifted by 5% EL.
source: Illumination carried out before n.c. 11 results in a recovery of the shape of the Hb gradient when comparing to that of dark conditions, although the posterior border is still anteriorly shifted by 5% EL (Figure 5D, ⑧ and 5E–F, anterior shift indicated by red dashed line).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Hb expression shown in Figure 5D and 5E-F.

claim: The Bcd inputs during n.c. 10–12 are integrated into later decisions on boundary positions.
source: This suggests that the Bcd inputs during n.c. 10–12 are integrated into later decisions on boundary positions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that illumination before n.c. 11 results in an anteriorly shifted Hb posterior border.

claim: The anterior boundary of Kr shows very high sensitivity to Bcd transcriptional inhibition - 20 min of illumination during the end of n.c. 14 causes an anterior shift by 3% EL.
source: We find that the anterior boundary of Kr shows very high sensitivity to Bcd transcriptional inhibition - 20 min of illumination during the end of n.c. 14 causes an anterior shift by 3% EL, slightly widening the Kr domain (Figure 5G, ②, blue dot).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Kr expression shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Both the anterior and posterior borders of the Kr expression domain shift anteriorly upon illumination conditions ④, ⑤ and ⑥.
source: Both the anterior and posterior borders of the Kr expression domain shift anteriorly upon illumination conditions ④, ⑤ and ⑥ (Figure 5G), correlating with the shift of the Hb boundary (Figure 5B, ④ and 5C, ⑤ and ⑥).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Kr expression shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The Kni anterior boundary shifts in correspondence with the posterior Kr boundary shifts, while its posterior boundary is much less sensitive.
source: The Kni anterior boundary shifts in correspondence with the posterior Kr boundary shifts, while its posterior boundary is much less sensitive (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of Kni expression shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The more anterior expression boundaries are located, the more susceptible they are to temporal inhibition of Bcd-dependent transcription.
source: In summary we find that the more anterior expression boundaries are located, the more susceptible they are to temporal inhibition of Bcd-dependent transcription.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the quantitative analysis of gap gene expression.

claim: A tight temporal interplay between Bcd and Hb is required for the precise positioning of gap gene expression boundaries.
source: Further, we find that a tight temporal interplay between Bcd and Hb is required for the precise positioning of gap gene expression boundaries.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the quantitative analysis of gap gene expression.

claim: A minimal 20 min illumination at the end of n.c. 14 abolishes the expression of the Knirps anterior domain (Kni1) capping the tip of the embryo.
source: A minimal 20 min illumination at the end of n.c. 14 abolishes the expression of the Knirps anterior domain (Kni1) capping the tip of the embryo (Figure 6B and B'), as well as the first Giant stripe (Gt1) (Figure 6C and C').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6B and B'.

claim: A minimal 20 min illumination at the end of n.c. 14 abolishes the expression of the first Giant stripe (Gt1).
source: A minimal 20 min illumination at the end of n.c. 14 abolishes the expression of the Knirps anterior domain (Kni1) capping the tip of the embryo (Figure 6B and B'), as well as the first Giant stripe (Gt1) (Figure 6C and C').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6C and C'.

claim: Extending the Bcd inactivation across n.c. 14 further inhibits the gap gene expression domains located slightly more posterior, Orthodenticle (Otd) and the second Gt stripe (Gt2).
source: Extending the Bcd inactivation across n.c. 14 further inhibits the gap gene expression domains located slightly more posterior, Orthodenticle (Otd) and the second Gt stripe (Gt2) (Figure 6C'', D and D').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6C'', D and D'.

claim: Recovery of transcription activity in late stages fails to rescue the expression of most anterior gap gene domains (Kni1, Gt1, Otd).
source: Recovery of transcription activity in late stages fails to rescue the expression of most of these anterior gap gene domains (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C6, D6 and F6).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C6, D6 and F6.

claim: When Bcd-dependent transcription is inhibited during n.c. 10–12 and then embryos returned to dark from n.c. 13, the time window for transcriptional recovery (approximately 1 hr) is insufficient to rescue the expression patterns of Kni1, Gt1 and Otd.
source: When Bcd-dependent transcription is inhibited during n.c. 10–12 and then embryos returned to dark from n.c. 13, the time window for transcriptional recovery (approximately 1 hr) is insufficient to rescue the expression patterns of Kni1, Gt1 and Otd (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C7, D7 and F7).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C7, D7 and F7.

claim: Bcd-dependent transcription serves a priming role prior to n.c. 13 to activate anterior segmentation genes at later stages.
source: This supports a mechanism whereby Bcd-dependent transcription serves a priming role prior to n.c. 13 to activate anterior segmentation genes at later stages.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that early illumination cannot be rescued by late recovery of Bcd activity.

claim: The priming role of Bcd-dependent transcription is stage-specific, as it is not compensated by late recovery of Bcd transcriptional activity.
source: Such a priming role is stage-specific, as it is not compensated by late recovery of Bcd transcriptional activity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that late recovery of Bcd activity cannot rescue early illumination effects.

claim: Illumination for 30 min before n.c. 10 has no apparent impact on segmentation gene expression.
source: In comparison, illumination for 30 min before n.c. 10 has no apparent impact on segmentation gene expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B8–G8), corroborating previous results (Figure 3) that Bcd-dependent transcription in this time window is dispensable for embryonic viability.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B8–G8.

claim: Bcd-dependent transcription in the time window before n.c. 10 is dispensable for embryonic viability.
source: In comparison, illumination for 30 min before n.c. 10 has no apparent impact on segmentation gene expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B8–G8), corroborating previous results (Figure 3) that Bcd-dependent transcription in this time window is dispensable for embryonic viability.
evidence: The claim is supported by cuticle preparation and immunostaining data.

claim: The reliance of the most anterior gap gene expression (Kni1, Gt1, and Otd) on persistent Bcd-dependent transcription may explain that inhibiting Bcd transcriptional activity both at very late or early stages impairs the proper formation of the anterior-most segments.
source: The reliance of the most anterior gap gene expression (Kni1, Gt1, and Otd) on persistent Bcd-dependent transcription may explain our previous observations that inhibiting Bcd transcriptional activity both at very late or early stages impairs the proper formation of the anterior-most segments (Figure 3D and L).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that anterior gap genes require persistent Bcd activity.

claim: Any short interruption of Bcd transcriptional activity (from n.c. 10 till the very end of n.c. 14) abolishes the activation or maintenance of the most anterior gap gene expression domains.
source: Any short interruption of Bcd transcriptional activity (from n.c. 10 till the very end of n.c. 14) abolishes the activation or maintenance of these gap gene expression domains.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: The expression of gap gene domains at posterior positions is less susceptible to perturbations in Bcd function.
source: Comparatively, the expression of gap gene domains at posterior positions is less susceptible to perturbations in Bcd function.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: The more anterior structures, which have cell fates governed by high Bcd concentration, require Bcd for an extended period of time.
source: The more anterior structures, which have cell fates governed by high Bcd concentration, require Bcd for an extended period of time.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: Cells at positions responding to low Bcd require a markedly shorter time window of exposure to Bcd activity to commit to cell fates appropriate for their spatial position.
source: On the contrary, cells at positions responding to low Bcd require a markedly shorter time window of exposure to Bcd activity to commit to cell fates appropriate for their spatial position.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: Bcd-dependent transcription not only determines the position of cephalic furrow invagination but also dictates the timing of when this tissue remodeling occurs.
source: For example, we find that Bcd-dependent transcription not only determines the position of cephalic furrow invagination (Vincent et al., 1997) but also dictates the timing of when this tissue remodeling occurs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by light-sheet microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: During mouse limb development, cells exposed to Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) morphogen for longer time develop into digits of more posterior identity.
source: They found that during mouse limb development, cells exposed to Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) morphogen for longer time develop into digits of more posterior identity (Harfe et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Harfe et al., 2004.

claim: In chick neural tube formation the duration of Shh activity is translated into different cell types along the dorso-ventral axis.
source: Similarly, in chick neural tube formation the duration of Shh activity is translated into different cell types along the dorso-ventral axis (Dessaud et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dessaud et al., 2007.

claim: In fish dorso-ventral patterning it is not the duration but the timing of BMP signaling that is important for correct cell fate determination.
source: In comparison, in fish dorso-ventral patterning it is not the duration but the timing of BMP signaling that is important for correct cell fate determination (Tucker et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tucker et al., 2008.

claim: In some cases the temporal integration of morphogen signaling is carried out by genetic feedback loops.
source: While in some cases the temporal integration of morphogen signaling is carried out by genetic feedback loops (Dessaud et al., 2010), in many other systems the underlying mechanism has not been unveiled.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dessaud et al., 2010.

claim: The blastoderm stage (from fertilization to the onset of gastrulation) spans 2.5 hr.
source: The blastoderm stage (from fertilization to the onset of gastrulation) spans 2.5 hr.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental measurements of developmental timing.

claim: The last syncytial cycle (n.c. 14), demarcated by the last division wave and the first sign of gastrulation, lasts about 45 min.
source: The last syncytial cycle (n.c. 14), demarcated by the last division wave and the first sign of gastrulation, lasts about 45 min.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental measurements of developmental timing.

claim: The penultimate cycle (n.c. 13) lasts 15 min.
source: The penultimate cycle (n.c. 13) lasts 15 min, while the duration of the previous three cycles (n.c. 10–12) is about 30 min in total.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental measurements of developmental timing.

claim: The duration of the previous three cycles (n.c. 10–12) is about 30 min in total.
source: The penultimate cycle (n.c. 13) lasts 15 min, while the duration of the previous three cycles (n.c. 10–12) is about 30 min in total.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental measurements of developmental timing.

claim: Illumination does not affect the normal Bcd diffusion.
source: Illumination does not affect the spatial distribution of the protein (Figure 1J), suggesting that the normal Bcd diffusion is not hampered.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Bcd spatial distribution is unchanged under illumination.

claim: CRY2::mCh::Bcd in light can specifically recognize and bind to the Bcd response element in the 3'UTR of Caudal mRNA.
source: The fact that CRY2::mCh::Bcd inhibits Cad translation in the anterior region of illuminated embryos suggests that CRY2::mCh::Bcd in light can specifically recognize and bind to the Bcd response element in the 3'UTR of Caudal mRNA.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Cad translation is inhibited in illuminated embryos.

claim: The homeodomain folding of CRY2::mCh::Bcd remains intact during illumination.
source: This indicates that the homeodomain folding remains intact during illumination.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that CRY2::mCh::Bcd can bind to Caudal mRNA in light.

claim: CRY2::mCh::Bcd in light still binds to its native DNA binding sites.
source: CRY2::mCh::Bcd competes with wild-type Bcd to inhibit target gene transcription in a dominant negative manner, indicating that CRY2::mCh::Bcd in light still binds to its native DNA binding sites.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that CRY2::mCh::Bcd acts in a dominant negative manner.

claim: Light-induced CRY2 conformational change does not alter Bcd specific DNA binding but abolishes its transcription activating potency due to the failure of proper assembly or the release of the transcriptional machinery.
source: Altogether, these results point to the scenario where light-induced CRY2 conformational change does not alter Bcd specific DNA binding but abolishes its transcription activating potency due to the failure of proper assembly or the release of the transcriptional machinery.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Three anterior embryonic regions with different sensitivity for bcd reduction can be distinguished: the preantennal head region, the antennal and gnathocephalic head segments, and the thorax.
source: Three anterior embryonic regions with different sensitivity for bcd reduction can be distinguished, that is, the preantennal head region, the antennal and gnathocephalic head segments, and the thorax.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about bcd hypomorphic alleles.

claim: The weakest bcd alleles only affect the preantennal head region.
source: While the weakest bcd alleles only affect the first region, defects sequentially extend to the second and third regions with increased allelic strength (Frohnhöfer and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1986).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Frohnhöfer and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1986.

claim: Defects sequentially extend to the antennal and gnathocephalic head segments, and the thorax with increased allelic strength of bcd.
source: While the weakest bcd alleles only affect the first region, defects sequentially extend to the second and third regions with increased allelic strength (Frohnhöfer and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1986).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Frohnhöfer and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1986.

claim: The same distinction of anterior embryonic regions can be made by temporally perturbing Bcd activity, with prolonged transcriptional inhibition giving rise to defects in sequentially extending regions.
source: Interestingly, the same distinction can be made by temporally perturbing Bcd activity, with prolonged transcriptional inhibition giving rise to defects in sequentially extending regions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: Constitutively low bcd activity is functionally equivalent to normal bcd activity with reduced active duration.
source: The resemblance between hypomorphic bcd alleles and short temporal perturbations demonstrates that constitutively low bcd activity is functionally equivalent to normal bcd activity with reduced active duration; both are sufficient to guide proper cell differentiation trajectories in the mid region of the embryo where target gene binding affinities are high.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison between hypomorphic alleles and temporal perturbations.

claim: In the more anterior region where target genes have low affinities, both wild-type level bcd activity and long duration are necessary for anterior induction.
source: In comparison, in the more anterior region where target genes have low affinities, both wild-type level bcd activity and long duration are necessary for anterior induction.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: Duplicated posterior structures only appear in strong allelic mutants but not in embryos subjected to long illumination due to a normal Cad gradient.
source: It is noteworthy that duplicated posterior structures only appear in strong allelic mutants but not in embryos subjected to long illumination due to a normal Cad gradient in our experiments.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations.

claim: In Drosophila - as in all long germband insects - the embryonic segments emerge simultaneously.
source: In Drosophila - as in all long germband insects - the embryonic segments emerge simultaneously (Sander, 1976).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sander, 1976.

claim: Bcd-dependent cell fate specification appears to move from posterior towards the anterior in a sequential manner.
source: Bcd-dependent cell fate specification appears to move from posterior towards the anterior in a sequential manner.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: The most posterior cells 'lock-in' to their correct fate decisions by early cycle 14, becoming refractory to further alterations of Bcd dosage.
source: The most posterior cells 'lock-in' to their correct fate decisions by early cycle 14, becoming refractory to further alterations of Bcd dosage.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: More anterior genes remain sensitive to Bcd dosage for much longer periods.
source: Meanwhile, more anterior genes remain sensitive to Bcd dosage for much longer periods.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal perturbation experiments.

claim: This mode of temporal interpretation can cope better with a temporally dynamic morphogen gradient or fluctuations in local concentration.
source: Therefore, this mode of temporal interpretation can cope better with a temporally dynamic morphogen gradient or fluctuations in local concentration.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the functional significance of the observed temporal pattern.

claim: This temporal sequence of boundary determination may help to assure robustness of gene boundary specification within such a short developmental time.
source: This temporal sequence of boundary determination may help to assure robustness of gene boundary specification within such a short developmental time.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the functional significance of the observed temporal pattern.

claim: The optogenetic manipulation shows fast kinetics with immediate inhibition of transcription upon illumination and re-initiation of transcription 5 min after returning to dark condition.
source: These observations suggest that the optogenetic manipulation shows fast kinetics with immediate inhibition of transcription upon illumination and re-initiation of transcription 5 min after returning to dark condition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from live imaging experiments of MS2 reporter.

claim: The measured PolII elongation rate is 1.54 kb/min.
source: Given that the MS2-yellow reporter gene is 6.4 kb in length and the measured PolII elongation rate is 1.54 kb/min (Garcia et al., 2013), we attribute the remnant reporter signals within these 4 min to the elongating transcripts initiated before illumination.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Garcia et al., 2013.

claim: Eve stripes 1 and 2 are Bcd-dependent and more posterior stripes are Bcd-independent.
source: We used the Even-skipped (Eve) pattern, where Eve stripes 1 and 2 are Bcd-dependent and more posterior stripes are Bcd-independent as a readout of Bcd activity (Frasch and Levine, 1987; Stanojevic et al., 1991).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Frasch and Levine, 1987 and Stanojevic et al., 1991.

claim: The inhibitory effect for the same genetic background and illumination conditions is uniform along the AP axis.
source: Further, the inhibitory effect for the same genetic background and illumination conditions is uniform along the AP axis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: A significant anterior shift of cephalic furrow position is observed in embryos illuminated during n.c.10–11 compared to dark condition (64.4 ± 1.5% EL in dark and 70.4 ± 1.3% EL in illuminated embryos).
source: Consistent with this, we observed a significant anterior shift of cephalic furrow position in embryos illuminated during n.c.10–11 compared to dark condition (64.4 ± 1.5% EL in dark and 70.4 ± 1.3% EL in illuminated embryos; Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by light-sheet microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The model reproduces the anterior shift in Kni and Kr boundaries upon deactivation of Bcd activity in n.c. 13 and early n.c. 14.
source: The model reproduces the anterior shift in Kni and Kr boundaries upon deactivation of Bcd activity in n.c. 13 and early n.c. 14 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by modeling results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The behaviour of the anterior domains of Hb and Gt are not consistent with the model predictions using the optimal parameter set.
source: However, the behaviour of the anterior domains of Hb and Gt are not consistent with the model predictions (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by modeling results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3B.

claim: 9 out of 21 parameter sets qualitatively agreed with at least three of the criteria derived from optogenetic perturbations.
source: We identified 9 out of 21 parameter sets that qualitatively agreed with at least three of the above criteria.
evidence: The claim is supported by modeling analysis.

claim: Bcd plays a more prominent role in activating Gt and Kni autoregulation is reduced in the parameter subset that agrees with optogenetic perturbations.
source: For example, Bcd plays a more prominent role in activating Gt and Kni autoregulation is reduced in the parameter subset.
evidence: The claim is supported by modeling analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3E.

claim: Temporal perturbations can be used to refine models of gap gene segmentation.
source: This suggests that our temporal perturbations can be used to refine models of gap gene segmentation and that gap gene network models need to incorporate Bcd dynamics as well as potential additional interactions within the anterior domain.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the modeling analysis.

claim: Gap gene network models need to incorporate Bcd dynamics as well as potential additional interactions within the anterior domain.
source: This suggests that our temporal perturbations can be used to refine models of gap gene segmentation and that gap gene network models need to incorporate Bcd dynamics as well as potential additional interactions within the anterior domain.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the modeling analysis.
